content:
Over the past few days, there have been two reports highlighting different paths for Apple to increase its profitability by boosting services revenue.

In my view, Apple absolutely should do the first one, but not the second — and it seems Phil Schiller would agree with that take…

Let me first summarise what those two reports say.

Home security & monitoring service

On Friday, Bloomberg reported that Apple may be planning to launch a brand-new home security & monitoring service, accompanying some long-awaited new home hardware.

Squeezing more money from the App Store

A second report published by the same source on Sunday suggested that the company is looking into ways to squeeze more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple should NOT do the latter

Put it this way: I think the second approach would be a huge mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly over iPhone app sales has already come under fire from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell iPhone apps, you're forced to do so via the official App Store, and you have no choice but to accept the company's terms — take it or leave it.

I know plenty of people will say no one is forcing you to buy an iPhone or develop apps for it, but that isn't how even the most laissez-faire version of capitalism actually works: even the US has had antitrust laws since 1890. Once you achieve a certain level of market dominance, restrictions are imposed on your behaviour to ensure you don't abuse your position.

Trying to squeeze more money out of the App Store is the polar opposite of "skating to where the puck is going" — and Schiller is reportedly on the same page, with Bloomberg citing it as one of the reasons for his stepping back now.

Innovative services are the right direction

By contrast, launching innovative new services that people want to buy is precisely what Apple should be doing. I can easily see the value in the company offering a home security monitoring service.

I said back in 2024 that making its own smart home cameras would be one of the smartest things the company could do. I said the same when rumours swirled about an Apple smart doorbell. Adding an optional service bundle to security products makes complete sense, for two reasons.

First, there are all the privacy arguments I've made before. HomeKit Secure Video already goes a long way towards ensuring the privacy of security camera footage. If there's one company I'd be comfortable letting use AI to analyse security camera footage, it's Apple.

Second, Apple is of course best placed to integrate security hardware and services fully within the HomeKit ecosystem. I'm sure there are plenty of other areas where Apple could offer a similar advantage.

For me, the key is that Apple needs to apply the same attitude to services that it does to hardware. Make outstanding products that people are happy — even delighted — to pay for. Rather than squeezing money in ways that turn off customers, developers, and regulators alike.

What are your thoughts? Feel free to share your views in the comments.
